title: The Covenant of Grace
definition: The Covenant of Grace is God's gracious saving arrangement by which He promises life and redemption through Christ to sinners.
summary: The Covenant of Grace describes God's unified plan to save sinners through Christ across redemptive history.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the mediator and fulfillment of God's covenant promises.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine shows that salvation has always rested on God's gracious promise, ultimately fulfilled in Jesus. From the first promise of redemption to the finished work of Christ, God saves by grace through the Mediator He provides. It helps believers read the Bible as one unfolding story of rescue.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because it keeps the Old and New Testaments from being treated as separate plans of salvation. God's grace is consistent, covenantal, and Christ-centered. It strengthens confidence that God keeps every saving promise He makes.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Look for Christ and God's promise as you read the whole Bible. Trust the faithfulness of God when His promises seem slow. Teach salvation as one gracious story centered on Jesus.
